# Original Unit 3 optional practice
Try eight short tasks and two extended tasks at your own pace, or allow around 40 minutes for optional pacing practice. Use the stimulus and show your reasoning. These original questions are ungraded and are not an official examination paper.

## S1 
Trace the stock code in the stimulus. Give both final dictionaries  and explain why the snapshot is unchanged.

## S2 
Records A03:2,A01:1,A02:2 are insertion-sorted stably by quantity. Give final ID order, explain equal-key order  and justify whether ID binary search is valid directly.

## S3 
A binary-search loop uses low < high with inclusive endpoints. Identify the boundary repair; give a smallest revealing test and expected result; state the sorted-key precondition.

## S4 
Explain an overridden label() in Camera and Projector subclasses, a polymorphic call  and a repeated-return stock test.

## S5 
For 192.168.80.34/27 give mask, network, broadcast and ordinary capacity.

## S6 
For a remote server with no NAT, explain remote IP destination and local next-hop MAC. Compare TCP reliability with UDP and state an encryption caveat.

## S7 
15 clients need 8 Mbit/s each over 100 Mbit/s: demand and bottleneck.300 MB at 100 Mbit/s: ideal time  and one limitation.

## S8 
Explain why routed VLANs alone do not enforce a guest restriction. Interpret unanswered middle traceroute probes followed by a responding destination.

## E1 
Design available_ids(records): return the unique IDs with quantity>0, in input order, without modifying records. Records are valid (unique string ID,non-negative integer quantity) pairs. Write code/pseudocode; give empty,zero and mixed tests with expected outputs; explain dictionary versus list choice for repeated ID lookup.

## E2 
Allocate 192.168.90.0/24 to Studio 45endpoints+gateway, Staff 20+gateway, Devices 9+gateway, Guests 5+gateway. Give each smallest ordinary LAN prefix; aligned nonoverlapping allocation; one correct gateway per group; explain where guest restriction is enforced; identify a required narrow service dependency.
